forward_guidance.text: The 10-K contains no quantitative revenue, margin, EPS or ARR guidance for fiscal 2027 or the upcoming quarter (Q1 FY2027, ending October 31, 2026). Qualitative statements and forward indicators: about 9.3 billion of the 21.2 billion RPO is expected to be recognized within 12 months; operating expenses are expected to increase in absolute dollars; about 3.3 billion of unrecognized share-based compensation will be recognized over about 2.5 years; the CyberArk workforce optimization plan (60 million estimated cost) should be substantially complete by end of FY2027; seasonality is expected to be strongest in fiscal Q2 and Q4; Embrace (completed Aug 27, 2026) and Console (completed Sept 1, 2026) will be accounted for as business combinations in Q1 FY2027.
forward_guidance.source_citation: 10-K Note 2 Revenue (RPO); Item 7 MD&A, Operating Expenses; Note 8 Acquisitions; Note 20 Subsequent Events; Item 1 Seasonality

bull_case: Revenue grew 24% to 11.5B, and NGS ARR rose to 9.1B from 5.6B (10-K Item 7).
RPO of 21.2B (up from 15.8B), with about 9.3B recognizable in 12 months, gives visibility (Note 2).
Operating cash flow of 4.55B and FCF of 4.11B (about 36% of revenue) show strong cash generation despite thin GAAP operating margin (Item 7).

The platform has been broadened through CyberArk (identity), Chronosphere (observability), Koi, Portkey, Embrace and Console, positioning the company in AI security (Prisma AIRS) and agent identity (Item 1).
Growth is broad across theaters, with EMEA up 27% and APAC up 25% (Item 7).
7.9B of cash and investments and an undrawn 400M revolver support liquidity; ICFR was effective with an unqualified audit opinion (Item 7; Item 9A).
bear_case: GAAP profitability compressed: operating margin 6.1% versus 13.5%, net income down 73% and diluted EPS 0.40 versus 1.60, with a 42.7% tax rate (Item 7; Note 16).
Gross margin fell about 300 bps to 70.4% on intangible amortization, cloud costs and memory/component inflation that may persist (Item 7; Item 1A).
The acquired businesses contributed 930M of revenue but an 797M operating loss; integration, retention and synergy risk is high, and 22B of goodwill is exposed to impairment (Note 8; Note 9).
The 2030 Notes (about 1.1B principal, 1.8B fair value) and Capped Calls will keep GAAP other income volatile and may require cash settlement (Note 11).
Usage-based revenue can see optimization pullbacks, and hyperscalers and frontier AI vendors are entering security and observability (Item 1A).
Concentration: two distributors were 30% of revenue, and 8.2B of purchase commitments are fixed regardless of demand (Item 1A; Note 13).
A PAN-OS authentication bypass vulnerability disclosed in May 2026 raises product-quality and reputational concerns (Item 1A).

what_to_watch.text: Q1 FY2027 (quarter ending Oct 31, 2026) is the first full quarter with CyberArk and Chronosphere; the 10-K notes seasonality with strongest sequential growth in fiscal Q2 and Q4, so check sequential revenue and NGS ARR trajectory versus the 9.1B year-end level.
Gross margin trajectory: whether it stabilizes near 70% or falls further on memory/component costs, cloud hosting costs and intangible amortization (about 1.08B of amortization scheduled for FY2027).
Operating expenses and the pace of the CyberArk workforce optimization plan (60M total cost, 14M severance liability at year-end), plus Embrace (325M) and Console (500M) integration costs.
Management commentary on consumption-based revenue optimization in observability and AI-related offerings.

Fair value moves in the 2030 Notes and Capped Calls (driven by the stock price) and their effect on GAAP other income and the tax rate; whether the 280.75 sale-price conversion condition is met in the calendar quarter ending September 30, 2026.
Capital allocation: the 1.0B remaining repurchase authorization expires Dec 31, 2026, and none was repurchased in the quarter ended July 31, 2026.
Centripetal appeal (114M judgment plus interest), the Finjan appeal, and the IBM QRadar transition services arrangement ending in the quarter ending Oct 31, 2026.
Customer response to the May 2026 PAN-OS vulnerability and demand for the new Prisma AIRS (including AIRS Gateway), Cortex XSIAM and Idira platforms.

data_gaps: No quarterly (10-Q) or earnings-release data was provided, so Q1 FY2027 comparables, quarterly NGS ARR and sequential trends cannot be cited.
No formal company guidance (revenue, EPS, margin, ARR, FCF) was provided; the 10-K contains none, so forward_guidance contains only qualitative indicators.
No analyst consensus estimates were provided.
No news articles or URLs were provided, so recent_news is empty.
The prior-year 10-K was not provided, so the is_new flags on risks are inferred from the FY2026 text and events (CyberArk, memory shortage, PAN-OS vulnerability) rather than a direct comparison.
Non-GAAP operating margin and non-GAAP EPS are not in the 10-K (only free cash flow is reconciled), though the company uses non-GAAP net income per diluted share as a PSU performance condition.
Revenue contribution from Chronosphere and CyberArk is disclosed only in combination (930M); CyberArk alone is only given as 6% of consolidated revenue.
No billings or calculated billings figure is disclosed in the 10-K.
The MD&A geographic table shows total revenue growth of 25% while other sections show 24% (2,259 / 9,221 is about 24.5%); the 24% figure is used throughout.

hypotheses_explored.question: Will gross margin pressure persist into the Q1 FY2027 print?
hypotheses_explored.summary: Gross margin fell about 300 bps in FY2026 on acquisition amortization, cloud costs and Q4 memory/component inflation. The 10-K says these cost pressures could continue, and the full-quarter inclusion of acquired intangibles (about 1.08B FY2027 amortization versus 640M in FY2026) points to more pressure near term.
evidence_quotes: we experienced supply chain disruption and inflationary pressures during our fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, resulting in increased costs for memory and other components, which have negatively affected our gross margin and could continue to affect our gross margin.

Subscription and support gross margin decreased for fiscal 2026 compared to fiscal 2025 primarily due to higher amortization of intangible assets as a result of our acquisitions in our current fiscal year and an increase in costs related to our cloud-based offerings.

hypotheses_explored.question: How much of the NGS ARR increase to 9.1B is organic versus acquired?
hypotheses_explored.summary: NGS ARR rose from 5.6B to 9.1B, but the company says the metric's scope expands when it acquires products, and CyberArk and Chronosphere were added mid-year. The 10-K gives no organic split, so headline ARR growth likely overstates organic momentum, which matters for evaluating the next print.
evidence_quotes: The scope of products, subscriptions, and support offerings that contribute to NGS ARR will generally increase over time as we introduce or acquire new next-generation products, subscriptions, and support offerings.

hypotheses_explored.question: Is the 2030 Notes cash-settlement exposure a near-term liquidity concern?
hypotheses_explored.summary: The notes are about 1.1B principal against 7.9B of cash and investments, and the sale-price conversion condition was not met in the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Liquidity looks ample; the main impact is GAAP volatility from fair value changes rather than a funding risk.
evidence_quotes: The sale price condition for the 2030 Notes was not met during the calendar quarter ended June 30, 2026, and as a result, our 2030 Notes are not convertible pursuant to that condition during the calendar quarter ending September 30, 2026.
